- Cache coherence
- Invalidation strategies (push vs TTL)

- Testing via chaos engineering

```lua
local key = KEYS[1]
local v = ARGV[1]
local cur = redis.call('GET', key)
if not cur or tonumber(cur) < tonumber(v) then
  redis.call('SET', key, v)
  redis.call('PUBLISH','cache_invalidate', key)
  return 1
end
return 0
```

The question probes depth in real-time data systems, focusing on cca analytics under high throughput, with late data and dedup—areas critical at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Streaming architectures with per-user keys, watermarking, late-arrival handling
- Exactly-once sinks, idempotent writes, dedup stores
- Backfill/replay, fault-injection testing, clock skew

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-code: dedup guard on incoming event
function handleEvent(e) {
  if (dedupStore.has(e.event_id)) return;
  dedupStore.add(e.event_id);
  sink.write(e); // idempotent downstream write
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate exactly-once guarantees under network partitions?
- What are trade-offs of in-memory dedup vs persistent dedup stores?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design privacy-aware, multi-tenant real-time scoring at scale with deterministic routing and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant isolation in streaming
- Data encryption at rest/in transit
- Canary rollout with per-tenant routing
- Observability and rollback criteria

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: per-tenant partitioning hash
function tenantPartition(tenantId, partitions) {
  const h = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(tenantId).digest('hex');
  return parseInt(h.slice(0, 8), 16) % partitions;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test rollback under sudden latency spikes?
- How do you verify that no tenant data leaks across partitions?

## Why This Is Asked
This probes privacy, security, and multi-tenant isolation in a live scoring pipeline, plus operational testing.

## Key Concepts
- Confidential computing (TEE/SGX)
- Envelope encryption and KMS/HSM
- Tenant isolation and per-tenant keys
- Auditability and drift detection
- Performance trade-offs under enclave overhead

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: encrypt, send to enclave, compute score, decrypt result
const payload = { userId, features };
const enc = kms.encryptEnvelope(payload, tenantId);
const score = enclave.computeScore(enc);
const result = kms.decryptEnvelope(score);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test isolation and key rotation?
- How do you detect compromised enclaves and trigger rollback?
